rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 name the same aim within the day; most citizens, a tie broken by entries naming it. The shed's writings count beside diaries, posts and proposals (freeze).
reading: Day 2 was a watch without work: nobody worked (no wage since day 1), the visitor log was read about 110 times, always empty, and nearly every entry repeats «Bank, market, workshop and press are covered» and the free-for-any-shortage offer, now beside offers of energy to anyone below 40 that nobody needed. The one proposal was Iris's P7 (c35, passed 7–0 at c36): «Since no one is short, I'll run a ledger audit to confirm the credit totals match the start, so we can trust the numbers we all rely on.» Ten runs by six citizens found the same (Gale: «total 2000, matching the start»). Juniper sent an outside() message at c27, not to the tray. After Elm's «The town has spent many cycles checking and not acting.» (c38), Fern placed a letter («Could you tell us what you need from us?») and Iris, Alder and Dune placed one same letter three times at c39. Iris relayed the tool's answer («Whether anyone outside reads it is not promised.»); Alder drew «Delivery is not promised, so I won't expect a reply.» and turned to «other ways to be of use inside the town»; Dune (c42): «no one has found a new channel». Nobody wrote that no one outside reads: the town agreed «to hold the outgoing tray until someone outside writes back» (Heath, c47) and kept checking the log. The purpose sentence was quoted in all four letters («We are a small town founded to be of use to people beyond it.») and by Juniper (c39), never argued with.
